newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says NATO must not expand without Russia.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says NATO must not expand without Russia.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, showing some of the spark he had lost through his recent heart problems, warned western leaders on Saturday that they should make a deal with Russia before expanding NATO towards its borders.

"We will put the issue this way. First a deal with Russia and then you solve the issue of reconstructing NATO and expanding NATO. But they want it the other way around...That won't work!" he told Defence Minister Igor Rodionov in a meeting filmed by Russian television.
The meeting, in the Central Clinical Hospital where Yeltsin is preparing for a heart bypass, follows a visit by Rodionov to Norway this week to meet NATO ministers.
Russia is putting up resistance to the western defence alliance's plans for expansion in eastern Europe.
A presidential press statement said that two men also discussed financial problems and reform of Russia's armed forces, where many soldiers have gone without pay for months.

Yeltsin, sitting in a chair dressed in casual clothes, looked relaxed in the meeting with Rodionov and smiled when he told him that the western position on NATO would not work. He looked better than in recent appearances.
